newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish Match first-half profit jumps 33 percent.
newsitem.headline: Swedish Match first-half profit jumps 33 percent.

text.p: Swedish tobacco and lighter company Swedish Match said Tuesday its profit after financial items rose 33 percent in the first half of 1997, despite a decline in the cigarette market.

The company posted a profit of 758 million crowns ($94.6 million), compared with 572 million crowns ($71 million) a year ago and sales of 3.63 billion crowns ($453 million) vs. 3.58 billion ($447 million) in the first half of 1996.
Analysts expected the company to post a profit of 799 million crowns ($100 million) for the period.

Swedish Match said increased sales and higher prices of its moist snuff products helped compensate for a decline in cigarette sales. The division reported a 25 percent increase in operating profit at 232 million crowns ($29 million) compared with 186 million ($23 million), with sales of 505 million crowns ($63 million) against 422 million ($53 million).
